extracted.intended_audience: early-18th-century educated readers; parents, guardians, and those interested in manners, dancing, conversation, friendship, and poetic composition
extracted.subtask_short: advice on manners, dancing, and poetry
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of prescriptive essays offering standards for upbringing, behaviour, social intercourse, friendship, the value of commerce, and principles of poetic composition aimed at improving individuals' conduct and taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of physical and mental education
rubrics_metrics.description: The general Mistake among us in the Educating our Children, is, That in our Daughters we take care of their Persons and neglect their Minds: in our Sons we are so intent upon adorning their Minds, that we wholly neglect their Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents should not focus solely on a daughter's appearance nor solely on a son's mind; educate mind and body together so that 'Gesture follow Thought' and the Body may 'express the Virtues of the Mind.' Anti-pattern: producing admired-looking daughters with uneducated minds and timorous sons neglected physically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make gesture follow thought (natural carriage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true Art in this Case is, To make the Mind and Body improve together; and if possible, to make Gesture follow Thought, and not let Thought be employed upon Gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training (e.g., dancing) should produce natural elegance rather than mechanical or affected poses. Avoid forcing a 'fantastical Gravity of Behaviour' and prescribed postures that occupy the mind with mere gesture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-breeding vs. fine (affected) breeding
rubrics_metrics.description: I am afraid the young Girl is in a fair Way to be spoiled: ... let us have your Opinion of this fine thing called Fine Breeding; for I am afraid it differs too much from that plain thing called Good Breeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good-breeding = plain, natural ease and simple manners that give assurance in company; 'fine breeding' and mere addition of external lessons risk making an affected fop. Dancing-masters teach rules of carriage, but without one's own good judgement these lessons produce affectation rather than genuine breeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper scope of dancing instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: so much of Dancing at least as belongs to the Behaviour and an handsome Carriage of the Body, is extreamly useful, if not absolutely necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit dance-learning to what gives graceful comportment; avoid excess. Use dancing to gain assurance and ease in company, but do not let it become mere display or affectation beyond what is 'useful' for behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid indecorous or lascivious dance practices
rubrics_metrics.description: very great Abuses are crept into this Entertainment ... they very often made use of a most impudent and lascivious Step called Setting ... an impudent young Dog ... whisked her round cleverly above Ground ... saw further above her Shoe than I can think fit to acquaint you with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of specific steps and customs (e.g., 'Setting', 'kissing Dances', 'Moll Patley') that encourage familiarity and indecency. Guardians should intervene when dances encourage overly familiar handling between sexes. Country-dancing can be innocent, but many of its practices may produce 'very dangerous Consequences.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Country dancing: social utility but risk of familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: As for Country Dancing, it must indeed be confessed, that the great Familiarities between the two Sexes on this Occasion may sometimes produce very dangerous Consequences; ... as every one is more or less a Proficient in it, I would not Discountenance it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Country dancing is culturally widespread and can be practised innocently; its emblematical figures can teach modesty and discretion (e.g., 'Hunt the Squirrel' recommending Modesty). Nonetheless, supervise and moderate to avoid corruptions and excessive familiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of conversation depends on company size
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Multitude meet together upon any Subject of Discourse, their Debates are taken up chiefly with Forms and general Positions; ... the most open, instructive, and unreserved Discourse, is that which passes between two Persons who are familiar and intimate Friends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect superficial talk (weather, fashions, news) in large assemblies; more free, candid, and instructive discourse occurs in small, intimate company—especially between two close friends. Value intimate friendship for honest examination of opinions and feelings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and prove friends cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: 'That we should have many Well-wishers, but few Friends.' ... 'If thou wouldst get a Friend, prove him first, and be not hasty to credit him: For some Man is a Friend for his own Occasion...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not hasty trust; test friends over time. Keep many well-wishers but few true confidants. A new friend is 'as new Wine'—time reveals true worth. Prudence in selection avoids revealing secrets to the unworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of a good friend
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the several Qualifications of a good Friend, this wise Man has very justly singled out Constancy and Faithfulness as the principal: To these, others have added Virtue, Knowledge, Discretion, Equality in Age and Fortune, and ... Pleasantness of Temper. I should join ... a certain Æquability or Evenness of Behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek constancy, faithfulness, virtue, knowledge, discretion, similar age/fortune, pleasant temper, and evenness of humour. Avoid friends whose humours change wildly ('Difficilis, facilis...') since intermittent amiability and sudden ill-humour make living with them unstable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaches of friendship that are irrecoverable
rubrics_metrics.description: except for Upbraiding, or Pride, or disclosing of Secrets, or a treacherous Wound; for, for these things every Friend will depart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offences (disclosing secrets, pride, treachery) destroy friendship permanently; reviling or some wounds may be reconciled, but revealing confidences is unforgivable. Guard against behaviors that betray trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of thought and style as public virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: I know nothing which more shews the essential and inherent Perfection of Simplicity of Thought, above that which I call the Gothick Manner in Writing, than this, that the first pleases all Kinds of Palates, and the latter only such as have formed to themselves a wrong artificial Taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for simplicity and naturalness in writing; it pleases both ordinary and refined readers. Use plain, natural expressions rather than artificial epigrammatic or 'Gothick' affectations. Test audience reaction with ordinary people (Molière's old housekeeper as a litmus test).

rubrics_metrics.name: Heroic/epic poem should teach a moral precept suited to the country
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest Modern Criticks have laid it down as a Rule, that an Heroick Poem should be founded upon some important Precept of Morality, adapted to the Constitution of the Country in which the Poet writes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a central moral lesson that is relevant to the nation's constitution or prevailing social needs (e.g., Homer promoting union among Greek states). This moral framing gives civic utility to epic poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrate national persons and actions in epic subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The next Point observed by the greatest Heroic Poets, hath been to celebrate Persons and Actions which do Honour to their Country: ... The Poet before us has not only found out an Hero in his own Country, but raises the Reputation of it by several beautiful Incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epic subjects should glorify heroes and actions that enhance the nation's reputation; favor native heroes over remote or foreign mythic subjects. Anti-pattern: poets choosing irrelevant foreign exploits (Valerius Flaccus and Statius derided for subjects unconnected to Rome).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce's public value: mutual dependence and enrichment
rubrics_metrics.description: This grand Scene of Business gives me an infinite Variety of solid and substantial Entertainments. ... Nature seems to have taken a particular Care to disseminate her Blessings among the different Regions of the World, with an Eye to this mutual Intercourse and Traffick among Mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate commerce by how it knit nations together, supplies variety (foods, wares, luxuries), improves domestic life, creates wealth and employment, and augments national prosperity without expanding territory. Merchants are valuable members of commonwealth for enabling these benefits.
